entities.summary: Field Marshal Sir George Pollock, 1st Baronet, was a British Indian Army officer. He first saw action at the Battle of Deeg and at the Siege of Bhurtpore during the Second Anglo-Maratha War before taking part in the Anglo-Nepalese War. He also commanded the British artillery at the Battle of Prome and at Bagan during the First Anglo-Burmese War. Following a disastrous retreat from Kabul in January 1842 during the First Anglo-Afghan War, the retreating forces became stranded at the small British garrison at Jalalabad and Pollock was appointed Commander of the Force sent to relieve the garrison: he advanced through the Khyber Pass and relieved the garrison in April 1842.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: George Pollock's relief of Jalalabad in April 1842 prevented a potentially disastrous defeat for the British forces during the First Anglo-Afghan War, demonstrating his strategic leadership and saving thousands of lives.
